title: (fix) Treat a serialized exception from the address hierarchy endpoints as an error
body:

_Requested by **Ian Bacher, Pius Rubangakene** · [Slack thread](https://openmrs.slack.com/archives/C02UNMKFH8V/p1789733140211449?thread_ts=1789733140.211449&cid=C02UNMKFH8V)_

- [x] My work includes tests or is validated by existing tests.

## Summary

**Before.** The `addresshierarchy` module's `ajax/*.form` handlers are legacy Spring controllers, not part of the REST API, and they do not use HTTP status codes to report failure. When the module throws, they answer **HTTP 200 with the exception serialized as JSON** — an object with `message`, `localizedMessage`, `stackTrace` and `cause` — instead of the array of entries the frontend expects. They can also answer 200 with an empty or null body. Because the status is a success, SWR sets no error, so the hooks in `address-hierarchy.resource.tsx` ran `data?.data?.map(...)` either over `undefined` or over the exception object. That throws during render, and the whole registration form white-screens with `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'map')`.

**After.** All four addresshierarchy hooks go through a fetcher that validates the body. A 200 whose body is not the expected array is thrown, so SWR reports it through `error` and the components' existing error states render — `AddressComponent` shows its "Error occurred fetching ordered fields for address hierarchy" notification instead of crashing. The derived arrays also fall back to `[]`, so a malformed response can never throw at a consumer.

**How.** `fetchAddressHierarchyEntries` wraps `openmrsFetch` and inspects the parsed body. An array passes through unchanged. A non-array object carrying `message`/`localizedMessage` together with `stackTrace`/`cause` is recognised specifically as a serialized server exception, and the server's own `message` is surfaced in the thrown `Error` — that message is the only diagnostic this endpoint gives us, and it is what makes a report like this one actionable. The stack trace is deliberately not logged; a concise error is enough. Anything else that isn't an array (empty body, null, unexpected object) throws a generic "response body was not an array". Safe fallbacks were added at the three places the crash surfaced: the order map in `AddressComponent`, and the `findIndex` and `slice` calls in `useAddressEntryFetchConfig`.

This **replaces #2756**, which was reverted. The root-cause explanation has been corrected: that PR's code comment claimed the endpoint content-negotiates and can return an HTML page. That is not what happens — `openmrsFetch` sets `Accept: application/json` itself, so the app never sends a browser-style `Accept`, and the endpoint negotiates JSON correctly. The real mechanism, established from a HAR captured against a live server, is the 200-plus-serialized-exception response described above. The guard itself is still worth having, for the right reason.

This is the client-side half of the fix. The module bug behind the live reproduction is an unconfigured-hierarchy NPE whose empty cache map is then served as a success, fixed separately in openmrs/openmrs-module-addresshierarchy#66. Even with that landed, the frontend should not white-screen when a non-REST endpoint reports a failure inside a 200, which is what this PR addresses. As Ian noted in the thread, we cannot "fix" the HTTP codes this endpoint returns, and a REST version of these endpoints is worth sketching separately.
